correctness.rationale: Positive curvature measures obeying a constant rotated sum are absolutely continuous and bounded by c. At the two-valued endpoints any decomposition has the same curvature. Conversely a positive-measure simplex interior allows a three-cell two-moment-neutral perturbation preserving positivity, rotated sum, and support closure. The Fourier area formula is strictly concave on fixed mean and vanishing first harmonics; fixed-perimeter compactness guarantees a global minimizer, which must be extreme. The 3-order lens is checked independently by its geometric segment-area formula and Fourier consistency test. No numerical run is treated as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The complete primary Ou–Pan 2010 article introduces constant higher-order width, proves perimeter and Fourier properties, and states least-area as a question; it does not classify the infinite-dimensional Minkowski extreme set. Kallay is known for ordinary width \(k=2\); the \(k\ge3\) claim needs a new simplex-field moment-null decomposition. Closest accessible curvature-flow and biwidth sources are logically different. A particularly plausible same-family specialist Zhang article remained inaccessible, so coverage risk is explicit rather than asserted absent.
residual_risks: The full specialist article by Deyan Zhang on constant higher-order width could contain an equivalent extreme-point classification; available abstracts do not decide the issue.
Older planar convexity results might express the same result using alternate language such as rotational Minkowski summands or curvature simplex selectors.
A result confined to finite Fourier degree does not itself cover the nonsmooth full family; related records warrant independent follow-up.

value.rationale: An exact structural description of all Minkowski extreme elements for every \(k\ge3\) constrains an open generalized Blaschke–Lebesgue problem. The two first-Fourier closure constraints make local simplex extremality insufficient without constructing moment-preserving perturbations. It works for arbitrary nonsmooth bodies and identifies necessary geometry of every global area minimizer; the explicit \(k=3\) lens provides a meaningful nonsmooth feasible benchmark but is not asserted optimal.
